question: Which hormonal event directly triggers ovulation in the normal menstrual cycle?

answers.text: A sustained rise in FSH from the anterior pituitary

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: FSH drives follicular growth but does not directly trigger ovulation. The LH surge is the trigger.

answers.text: A midcycle surge in LH from the anterior pituitary

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! The midcycle LH surge (triggered by oestradiol positive feedback on the anterior pituitary) causes the dominant follicle to rupture and release the secondary oocyte approximately 36–40 hours later.

answers.text: A fall in progesterone from the corpus luteum

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A fall in progesterone triggers menstruation (if no implantation), not ovulation. Ovulation occurs in the mid-follicular phase, well before significant progesterone rises.

answers.text: A rise in prolactin from the posterior pituitary

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Prolactin is from the anterior pituitary and its role is in lactation. Hyperprolactinaemia actually inhibits ovulation by suppressing GnRH.

overallFeedback.feedback: The midcycle LH surge is the proximate trigger for ovulation, occurring ~36–40 hours before follicle rupture.
Correct! The LH surge occurs approximately 36–40 hours before ovulation and is the basis for urine LH-detection ovulation predictor kits.
